scope: Offline static analysis of the exact stock A6L (HLTE730T) kernel and vendor HWC. No hardware access, no writes, no ioctls. ELF virtual (link-time) addresses, not file offsets.

kernel_symbolized_elf.note: reconstructed analysis ELF (vmlinux-to-elf), text base 0xffffff8008080000; not the original vmlinux

char_device.name: epd_flash
char_device.created_via: class_create + device_create in epd_spi_probe (class stored in epd_flash_data->[0x8])

fops.write: epd_spi_write @ 0xffffff80084c3f60 (returns 0; NO side effect - a stub)
fops.unlocked_ioctl: NULL - no ioctl interface exists on this node

selinux.note: No domain is granted write on /dev/epd_flash; the write fop is a stub anyway. All persistent VCOM writes go through the fb1/epd_vcom sysfs -> kernel epd_write_vcom path.

epd_spi_read.buffer: vmalloc(0x70080) cached in epd_flash_data->[0x78], memset 0 before each read, vfree after
epd_spi_read.user_copy: __arch_copy_to_user, fixed 0x70080 bytes, with access_ok bounds check on (user_addr + 0x70080)
epd_spi_read.return_value: copy_to_user residual (0 on full success) - NOT a byte count
epd_spi_read.side_effects: asserts EPD power GPIOs high then low; allocates/frees vmalloc; issues real SPI transaction. Read is non-destructive to flash contents.

epd_read_vcom.side_effects: asserts epd_pwr_on GPIO high (flash power flag @ ctrl+0x935 set); non-destructive to flash

epd_write_vcom.input_validation: accepts vcom in [2000,3000] mV; else logs 'vcom is invalid' and returns -1 without touching flash
sequence: epd_spi_write_wrsr (opcode 0x01 + 1 data byte) -- unprotect status register
vmalloc(0x104); read existing 256 bytes at 0x070000 (opcode 0x03) into data area
overwrite 3 digit bytes at data offsets 0x11/0x13/0x14 with new vcom digits
epd_spi_set_wren; PAGE PROGRAM (opcode 0x02) 256 bytes at 0x070000; epd_wait_wip_clean
epd_write_vcom.destructive_scope: erases the 4 KiB sector at 0x070000; only 256 bytes (0x070000..0x0700FF) are re-programmed. Bytes 0x070100..0x070FFF in that sector are erased to 0xFF and NOT restored.

write_capable_paths.note: These opcodes exist ONLY inside epd_write_vcom's call graph (epd_spi_set_wren/epd_spi_write_wrsr/epd_wait_wip_clean and inline erase/program). They are not reachable through /dev/epd_flash (whose write fop is a stub and whose ioctl is NULL). They are reachable ONLY through the fb1/epd_vcom sysfs store.

mdss_epd_power_up.guard: requires mdss_dsi_res populated and ctrl_pdata->[0x18] non-null; early-returns (no-op, printk) otherwise; also gated by ctrl+0x198

mdss_epd_flash_power_on.sets_flag: ctrl+0x935 = 1 (prevents mdss_dsi_panel_power_ctrl from dropping epd_pwr_on during a flash op)

mdss_epd_flash_power_release.action: clears ctrl+0x935 = 0; does NOT drop the GPIO itself

vcom_two_stores.persistent_digital_vcom: SPI flash @ 0x070000 (read by epd_read_vcom, written by epd_write_vcom)

volatile_pmic_vcom.device: TI TPS65185 PMIC on i2c-2 @ 0x68 (/soc/i2c@c176000, node tps65185@68)
volatile_pmic_vcom.hwc_writer: HWCDisplayExternalEpd::SetEpdVcom opens that i2c vcom node O_RDWR and writes "%d"

ReadEpdFlash(void*, size_t).reads: read(fd, buf, count) once; returns byte count (>0) on success, 0 on error path
ReadEpdFlash(void*, size_t).note: This is the ONLY stock userspace reader of /dev/epd_flash.

EinkSwTconInit().behavior: malloc(0x70080); memset; ReadEpdFlash(buf, 0x70080); Init_Eink_SWTcon(this+0x4f8, mode=5, cfg@sp, buf, 0x70080, out=this+0x5a4); SetEpdVcom(this+0x660); SaveEpdInfo(); frees buf
EinkSwTconInit().significance: Confirms the 0x70080 flash window is the WAVEFORM data consumed by the software TCON. The request length exactly matches the kernel's fixed read length.

SetEpdVcom(uint).note: runtime PMIC VCOM, not the flash copy

unresolved_or_untested: JEDEC ID / RDID (0x9F) is never issued by the stock kernel; chip identity and true total capacity are unknown from static analysis.
Whether flash content beyond 0x070080 exists or matters; the fixed read never reaches it and no other opcode with a higher address was found.
Whether the 0x2B opcode in epd_write_vcom is a read-security-register or a vendor-specific op; only its 1-in/1-out shape is proven.
Live device-tree/overlay selection and whether the ed052tc2 SPI node is enabled at runtime on the modern port.
